answer: Each epoch, grading panels are drawn at random from a rotating validator pool, seeded from an on-chain anchor block hash so no panel can be bribed ahead. Reputation flows only when the current panel confirms a result, and panels rotate at the zenith of each epoch, so a sybil never knows which fakes sit together. To profit, an attacker must control a large random share of every future panel, and each identity adds staking cost and slashing risk. Collusion finds no harbor: identities are costly and re-audited, so fakes lose to honest agents.
